text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Activists from the Latvian Environmental Protection Club organised a protest near the ministry of agriculture and the ministry of environmental protection urging them to ensure that unused agricultural chemicals be stored in a safe place.
- Sweden will be the co-ordinator of foreign assistance to Latvia to create a refugee camp.
- The Latvian language test presents no problem for those applying for citizenship, according to an opinion poll carried out by the naturalisation board.
- President Guntis Ulmanis gave credentials to three Latvian ambassadors: Sandra Kalniete (France), Martins Perts (Italy) and Imants Liegis (Benilux).
- The cabinet approved Latvia's ratification of the 1951 Convention on Refugees.
- The Polish government approved a free trade agreement with Latvia on Tuesday, paving the way for Latvia to eventually become a member of the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA).
- The naturalisation board reports a ten percent increase in the number of naturalised persons over the first quarter of 1997 (670).
- Pensions in Latvia will increase by an average of 2.16 lats from May 1 to 42.84 lats.
- Andris Shkele believes Latvia is ahead of its neighbours in the field of privatisation, as well as in the field of tariff and price policies.
- Latvia's Association of Commercial Banks produced a Euromoney-based three-class rating of commercial banks, which is topped by Parex, Latvia's Universal Bank and Rietumu Banka.
- A former advisor to prime minister Maris Gailis, Eizens Cepurnieks, was appointed vice-president of Vereinsbank Riga.
